papers.title_en: International society of sports nutrition position stand: nutrition and weight cut strategies for mixed martial arts and other combat sports
papers.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
papers.tldr_en: An official position on nutritional and weight cut strategies for combat sports is developed and the long-term effects of frequent weight cuts on health and performance are unknown, necessitating further research.
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Following an extensive literature review, the International Society of Sports Nutrition (ISSN) has developed an official position on nutritional and weight cut strategies for combat sports. The type of combat sport, length of the fight camp, and time between weigh-in and competition are factors influencing nutritional and weight cut strategies. The following 16 points constitute the Position Statement of the Society; the Research Committee has approved them. 1. Combat sports have differing weight categories, official weigh-in times, and competition frequencies, influencing the nutritional and weight cut strategies for training and competition. 2. As the duration of a combat match increases, >4 min, contribution of the aerobic system can rise to >70%, yet anaerobic alactic pathways and anaerobic glycolytic pathways support high-output bursts. 3. papers.title_en: A comprehensive review of the physiology and evidence base to guide the use of ergogenic and medical supplements for enhanced cycling performance
papers.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
papers.tldr_en: An evidence-informed approach underscores the synergistic relationship between nutrition, training and performance optimization in cycling by exploring personalized nutrition frameworks, interactions between multi-supplement protocols and the molecular mechanisms underpinning adaptation to endurance training and nutritional interventions.
papers.abstract_en: Abstract Background A growing body of evidence supports the use of supplements to enhance cycling performance through both direct and indirect mechanisms. Methods This review was informed by a structured literature search conducted in PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science for peer-reviewed studies published up to May 2025. Studies were included if they involved human participants, were published in English and evaluated outcomes related to endurance performance, recovery or physiological function. Results Direct enhancement with ergogenic supplements is primarily achieved via modulation of skeletal muscle energy metabolism. During exercise, adenosine triphosphate (ATP) resynthesis is driven by the phosphagen system, glycolysis, oxidative phosphorylation and beta-oxidation, with each system contributing according to the intensity and duration of the effort. papers.title_en: Global Trends in RCTs Related to High-Intensity Interval Training and its Multi-Dimensional Application: A PubMed Review – Based Bibliometric Analysis from 2000 to 2026
papers.tldr_en: The research trends of RCTs related to HIIT have expanded from a sports context to a metabolic, oncological, neurological, and cardiac population with a greater emphasis on treating patients suffering from cancer and stroke, however, further RCTs must consider large sample sizes and more standardized trials to achieve greater efficacy.
papers.abstract_en: Studies on high-intensity interval training (HIIT) have shifted from improving athletic performance to clinical interventions addressing various pathological conditions across diverse populations. However, the structure of its randomized controlled trials (RCTs) remains unmapped. The PubMed database was searched for human RCTs published between 2000 and 2026, yielding 694 eligible trials after screening. Biblioshiny and VOSviewer were used to identify publication growth, author and institutional collaboration networks, the most influential and contributing authors in HIIT-related RCTs, and thematic analyses of research hotspots and keywords based on their occurrence. The RCTs appeared in 247 journals, with an annual growth of 18.84%, a peak of 132 published RCTs in 2025 and 34.29% international co-authorship. papers.title_en: Clinical applications of wearable sensor-based gait analysis in athletes: a systematic review for injury prevention and rehabilitation
papers.journal: BMC Sports Science Medicine and Rehabilitation
papers.journal_tier: 康复医学2区/运动科学3区
papers.tldr_en: Evaluating the clinical efficacy of wearable sensor–based gait analysis for injury prevention in athletes, examining its role in rehabilitation monitoring and clinical decision-making, and identifying methodological limitations and future research priorities required for standardized clinical integration identifies key challenges.
papers.abstract_en: Gait analysis is fundamental for optimizing athletic performance and mitigating injury risks in sports medicine. While traditional laboratory assessments offer insights, the emergence of wearable sensor technology provides novel opportunities for objective, real-time gait evaluation in ecologically valid settings. This systematic review aims to (1) evaluate the clinical efficacy of wearable sensor–based gait analysis for injury prevention in athletes (2), examine its role in rehabilitation monitoring and clinical decision-making, and (3) identify methodological limitations and future research priorities required for standardized clinical integration. Adhering to PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a systematic search was conducted across MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, and Embase from inception to May 31st, 2025. papers.title_en: Building for the Future: A Systematic Review of the Effects of Eccentric Resistance Training on Measures of Physical Performance in Youth Athletes
papers.tldr_en: The findings of this systematic review support the inclusion of eccentric resistance training in youth athletes to improve measures of muscular strength, jump, sprint and change of direction performance.
papers.abstract_en: Background Eccentric resistance training is recognised as an effective stimulus for enhancing measures of muscular strength and power in adult populations; however, its value in youth athletes is currently not well understood. Objective The aim of this systematic review was to critically appraise the effects of eccentric resistance training on measures of physical performance (i.e. muscular strength, jump, sprint and change of direction) in youth athletes 18 years of age and under. Methods Original journal articles published between 1950 and June 2022 were retrieved from electronic search engines of PubMed, SPORTDiscus and Google Scholar’s advanced search option. papers.title_en: Effects of different dietary supplements combined with conditioning training on muscle strength, jump performance, sprint speed, and muscle mass in athletes: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
papers.tldr_en: Protein supplementation appears to be the most effective strategy for increasing muscular strength; β-alanine and creatine both improve jump performance, with β-alanine offering marginally superior effectiveness; and creatine is particularly beneficial for sprint speed.
papers.abstract_en: Background As dietary supplements have become integral to meeting athletes’ specialised nutritional requirements, research into their effects on performance has intensified. Yet inconsistent findings leave the efficacy of some supplements—most notably branched-chain amino acids and β-hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate (HMB)—open to debate. To clarify which products offer the greatest benefit, we undertook a systematic review and network meta-analysis aimed at identifying the supplements most effective for athletes, including protein, creatine, β-alanine, HMB, vitamin D, caffeine, and others.
